title: Cost, Search and Recursion
introduction: Two correct algorithms can behave very differently as their input grows.
learningOutcomes: Compare constant, linear and quadratic growth.
Explain the requirement for binary search.
Identify a recursive base case and progress step.

activities.question: Which search requires the data to be ordered?
activities.explanation: Binary search discards ordered halves, so it depends on an ordering invariant.

activities.question: A recursive algorithm needs a base case that stops further calls.
activities.explanation: Without a reachable base case, recursion continues until resources are exhausted.

activities.question: Which growth is usually preferable for large inputs?
options: Any growth because size never matters
Repeated full scans rather than one scan
activities.explanation: Linear work grows in direct proportion to input size, while quadratic work grows much faster.
